newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA MILITANTS, PRIESTS OPPOSE U.S. EVANGELIST.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA MILITANTS, PRIESTS OPPOSE U.S. EVANGELIST.

text.p: Young Bulgarian nationalists and bearded Orthodox priests carrying icons demonstrated on Wednesday at a conference of evangelical churches led by a U.S. pastor.

On Tuesday, police had to remove young nationalists of the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation (IMRO) who clashed with disciples at the start of the conference led by Ronald Schambach, 71, and organised by three small Bulgarian evangelical churches.
Priests singing a mass and carrying a banner reading: "No Orthodox religion - no Bulgaria" joined theology students and IMRO activists in the protest. Another banner read "Yankee go home".

"IMRO is categorically opposed to the National Christian Conference at the National Palace of Culture which is a cover for yet another cult rally," IMRO said in a statement. Many of those attending the conference were Gypsies, the group hardest hit by Bulgaria's economic crisis.

Chief Prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev issued a statement advising IMRO not to make trouble, but added: "Behind the facade of organised religion in Bulgaria, sects are operating which are dangerous not only locally but internationally."

The Bulgarian branch of IMRO claims descent from a turn of the century guerrilla movement fighting for a separate Macedonian state. Its young militants helped provide security for January protests against the former Socialist government.
